# bugs #4054: Struct arguments of the form *p are copied from the address that their first bytes form

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4054/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17200
- Recommended action: Confirm the choices under Decision, then apply the patch. Close this ticket and patches #516.
- Patch: [bugs-4054.patch](../../patches/bugs-4054.patch), commit [`9078784f9`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/9078784f963ec1277adfefb884fbe3fc8762ea9a). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

When the argument of a call is `*p` and the parameter is a struct or union, the code reads the
first bytes of `*p` and copies the argument from the address that these bytes form. On r17193,
trunk's `support/regression/tests/bug-4054.c` with its body enabled fails for stm8, ucz80, and five
of the six mcs51 variants. It passes for mcs51-medium.

The value of `*p` or `a[i]` of struct type is wrong for the same reason in the argument
`(e, *p)`, in `x = *p = y`, and as an operand of a conditional expression (#4163, #3857). Two more
faults were found for mcs51. The compiler rejects `f (p[i])` with error 129 when `p` is a generic
pointer. In the large model without `--stack-auto`, `f (g ())` with a function `g` that returns a
struct copies the argument from code memory.

## Cause

`geniCodeDerefPtr` in `src/SDCCicode.c` generates for `*p` the read through the pointer that a
scalar needs, also when the object is a struct or union. The code that uses a struct value treats
its operand as the address of the object, so it uses the bytes that were read as an address.

`geniCodeSEParms` replaces an argument `p[i]` of struct type by `p + i` to avoid that read. The
replacement was added in [r13294](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13294/), the fix for bug
#3368. `geniCodeParms` then casts the pointer to the kind that belongs to the storage class of
`p`, and for mcs51 the compiler reports error 129 for this cast when `p` is a generic pointer.

For functions that are not reentrant, `geniCodeParms` assigns the address of a struct argument to
the second parameter of `memcpy` without a conversion. The mcs51 code generator then takes the
address space of the generic pointer from the output class in the type of the address. That class
is wrong for the value of a call and for a pointer that is not generic.

## Fix

With the patch, `geniCodeDerefPtr` does not generate the read for a struct or union whose value is
needed. The value is a copy of the pointer in a temporary that has the type of the object and the
output class of the pointer's kind. The value of a variable or of a member has this form.
`geniCodeSEParms` does not replace `p[i]`, and `geniCodeParms` casts the address to the type of
the `memcpy` parameter. The patch enables the body of `bug-4054.c`.

## Decision

The replacement from r13294 is removed, because `geniCodeDerefPtr` gives `p[i]` the right value.
`bug-3368.c` passes with the patch.

The expression statement `*vp;` with a pointer to a volatile struct does not read the object. On
r17193, mcs51 in the large model reads one byte of the object for this statement. C leaves it to
the implementation what an access to a volatile object is. The alternative is a read of every byte
of the object.

The ticket patches #516 proposes a change in `geniCodeSEParms` alone. The two patches are compared
in its entry.

For mcs51, two regression tests change size in the small model (-1 and +2 bytes) and two in the
large model (+1 and +5 bytes). With `--stack-auto` in the large model, seven tests are 11 to 69
bytes smaller. The sizes for stm8 are unchanged. `bug-4054` grows because its body is enabled.

## Verification

The new `support/regression/tests/bug-4054-2.c` has the arguments `*p`, `**pp`, `*(p + i)`,
`*p++`, `*--p`, `(e, *p)`, and `va_arg`, indexed forms, the value of an assignment, the value of a
call, and for mcs51 `__xdata`, `__data`, `__idata`, and `__code` pointers. On r17193 it does not
compile for the six mcs51 variants because of error 129, and 18 of its 41 assertions fail for stm8
and for ucz80. With the patch both tests pass on the host, for the six mcs51 variants, for stm8,
and for ucz80.

With this patch, the patch for #4131, and the earlier patches of the series applied, the
regression suite passes for the host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80, and valdiag passes
for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. Other ports were not tested.

## Related

- #4163 and #3857 report operands of the form `*p` in a conditional expression. Their entries
  state what this patch corrects without the patch for #4131.
- #4131 reports the other faults of conditional expressions of struct type, which this patch does
  not correct.
